agree.reason: A cold lead investor gets an apology with no reason behind it and a promise with no date, then the unfilled '[Your plan: ...]' placeholder under Runway, so the email reads as unfinished and gives little reason to take the founder's calls again.

honest.reason: The figures are accurate (about 11 months of runway, nearly half of no-shows removed), but the claims that records vendors are bundling scheduling and that the lost chain is 'exactly the kind of clinic this is built for' go beyond what the brief supports.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out runway and the no-show reduction, but it doesn't show that the lost chain was about 13% of MRR, that clinic count rose by a net 5, or when cash runs out if MRR stays flat, and it leaves out the 6 clinics already committed to standalone reminders.

right_comparison.reason: It frames the choice fairly as competing with a free built-in scheduler versus selling alongside it, but it leaves out that two more customers paying $3,800 a month use the same records system, which is the real trend in the downside.

qualification.reason: 'Next quarter I'll report on...' gives no target, the runway plan is a blank placeholder, and the January 7 commitment and monthly one-pager are missing, so the reader has nothing to check against a date or number.

objections.reason: The investor's objection is the silence and whether it will happen again, but the email doesn't give the honest reason (flat numbers), a fixed next date, or the monthly-numbers offer, and it skips the obvious question of whether other customers on the same records system will leave.

fit.reason: It is a well-structured investor email under 500 words, but the [Company], [Your name] and runway-plan placeholders mean it can't be sent as it stands.
